title: Front alternatives for B2B support teams in 2026
summary: Outgrowing Front? Compare 7 Front alternatives, including Pylon, Help Scout, Zendesk, Intercom, Freshdesk, HubSpot, and Plain, by fit and price.
body_markdown:
Front is a strong collaborative inbox, and teams that live in email often love it. The question usually comes up when support grows into a real operation: tiered SLAs, account context, and customers asking in Slack Connect and Microsoft Teams. Wispr Flow hit that point. Samm Yates, Founding Head of Customer Experience, said: "I wasn't actually even able to measure any of the KPIs that I was interested in. Essentially we were just driving blind at that point." After moving from Front to Pylon, Wispr Flow reports 9x faster first response time and 4x support volume with minimal increase in headcount.


This guide covers 7 Front alternatives, where each fits, and what each costs to start.


Quick note on names: Intercom is the help desk, and Fin by Intercom is its AI agent. We use "Intercom" for the help desk and "Fin" for the agent below.


## Why teams look for a Front alternative


Front is built around the inbox. That's its strength. Front brings email, Slack, WhatsApp, SMS, and other conversations into a shared workspace, and it now connects Microsoft Teams channels too. Teams that need account-level SLAs, routing by customer tier, and investigation across product data often want a tool built around the account instead.


Channels depend on plan. Front's Starter plan supports a single channel type (email, chat, or SMS). Omnichannel starts on Professional, and native WhatsApp is a paid add-on on Professional and Enterprise.


AI is sold separately below Enterprise. Copilot is an add-on on Starter and Professional and included in Enterprise. Autopilot, Front's AI agent, is an add-on on every plan.


## What to look for in a Front alternative


- Slack and Microsoft Teams as customer channels, with conversations tracked as work, not just mirrored into an inbox.
- Account context: every contact, open issue, and CRM field for the company, visible to people and agents.
- Agents that start before your team does, gathering context and recommending next steps when an issue arrives.
- Reporting you can run in the product, including SLAs by tier.
- A migration path for contacts, conversations, teammates, and knowledge base content.


## The 7 best Front alternatives


### Pylon


**Best for:** B2B teams that support customers in Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, and chat, and need account context in every issue.


Pylon is the agentic support platform built for B2B. Slack Connect, Slack Community, email, the chat widget, Discord, WhatsApp, Telegram, SMS, and ticket forms are on every plan. Microsoft Teams and Google Chat are on Advanced and Enterprise. Conversations become issues in one inbox, linked to the account.


Where Front's Copilot helps a teammate with the conversation in front of them, Pylon's Automations start work when an issue arrives: they gather account context, check connected systems, and run Skills before someone opens it. Agents investigate issues before your team opens them, so your team starts with evidence and recommended next steps.


- Support Agent answers from your content, collects information, gathers internal context, and can resolve issues end to end.
- Assist Agent investigates issues, drafts replies, and takes actions using workspace context.
- Slack Agent lets teammates you give access to ask about a customer or take approved actions from Slack.
- Automations run on an event or schedule.
- Skills are reusable instructions that people and agents both run. Skills are on every plan and don't use credits.


Wispr Flow also cut onboarding and training for new support hires from 2-4 months to 1-2 weeks after the move.


**Pricing:** Professional is $89 per seat per month and Advanced is $139 per seat per month, on an annual contract. Enterprise is a custom quote. Agentic features run on credits, with a 5,000 credit minimum commitment. Pylon doesn't charge per issue. See Pylon pricing.


**Tradeoffs:** no free plan, a minimum seat count for new customers, and Microsoft Teams needs Advanced. If your main need is collaboration across personal and shared email inboxes, Front remains a strong fit.


**Migrating from Front:** the Front migration guide covers contacts, issues, teammates, users, and knowledge base articles and categories. Migrated conversations arrive closed. Across 300+ migrations from Zendesk, Intercom, and Salesforce, 90% finished in under 2 months. For a side-by-side, see Pylon vs Front.


### Help Scout


**Best for:** small teams that want a simpler email inbox.


Help Scout covers email, live chat, SMS, WhatsApp, Instagram, and Messenger on paid plans, with a free plan for up to 5 users. Its Slack integration sends notifications only. Envoy, its AI agent, is an add-on billed per resolution.


### Zendesk


**Best for:** large teams that want deep configuration and a big app ecosystem.


Zendesk's Suite plans bring email, messaging, phone, and social together and list messaging apps including WhatsApp and Slack. Plans include AI agents with a set number of automated resolutions per agent. See Pylon vs Zendesk.


### Intercom


**Best for:** product-led teams supporting customers in-app.


Intercom pairs Messenger live chat with a shared inbox, ticketing, and a help center. Fin bills per outcome, on Intercom or on another help desk. See Pylon vs Intercom.


### Freshdesk


**Best for:** teams that want classic ticketing at a low entry price.


Freshdesk includes ticketing, a shared inbox, a customer portal, and a knowledge base on every paid plan. Freddy AI Agent includes 500 free sessions once per account. Its Slack app can create tickets from Slack messages.


### HubSpot Service Hub


**Best for:** teams that run sales and marketing on HubSpot.


Service Hub's help desk connects chat, email, forms, calling, WhatsApp, and Facebook Messenger next to CRM records. Customer Agent is on Professional and runs on HubSpot Credits.


### Plain


**Best for:** technical B2B teams that support customers in Slack.


Plain's Foundation plan includes Slack, email, and in-app channels and AI agents on monthly credits. Microsoft Teams is on Horizon. See Pylon vs Plain.

## Which Front alternative is right for you?


Stay on Front if your team's work is mostly collaborative email. Pick Help Scout for a simpler inbox, HubSpot Service Hub if your CRM is HubSpot, and Pylon if customers live in Slack and Teams and every issue needs account context.[Book a demo](https://www.usepylon.com/get-started) .


## FAQ


### What is the best Front alternative for B2B support?


For B2B teams that support customers in Slack, Microsoft Teams, and email and need account context in every issue, Pylon is built for that. Help Scout fits small teams that want a simpler inbox, and HubSpot Service Hub fits teams on HubSpot's CRM.


### Does Front support Slack and Microsoft Teams?


Yes. Front can read and reply to Slack messages from public and private channels, and it can connect Microsoft Teams channels to a Front inbox. Front supports Teams channel messages only, not direct messages or group chats.


### How is Pylon priced compared with Front?


Pylon Professional is $89 per seat per month and Advanced is $139 per seat per month, on an annual contract. Enterprise is a custom quote. Agentic features run on credits, and Pylon doesn't charge per issue. Front starts at $25 per seat per month billed annually, with Copilot and Autopilot sold as add-ons below Enterprise.


### How long does it take to migrate from Front to Pylon?


It depends on your channels, integrations, inbox structure, and history. Across 300+ migrations from Zendesk, Intercom, and Salesforce, 90% finished in under 2 months. Pylon's Front migration guide covers contacts, conversations, teammates, users, and knowledge base content.


### Has anyone moved from Front to Pylon?


Yes. Wispr Flow moved from Front to Pylon and reports 9x faster first response time and 4x support volume with minimal increase in headcount.
